category: Computer Vision Toolbox > Features, Detection, Calibration & 3-D
description: Feature detection and matching, object detection and deep-learning segmentation, image annotation, optical flow, camera and stereo calibration, point cloud processing, and OCR and barcode reading.

tools.name: detectSURFFeatures
tools.description: Detect blob-like interest points using the Speeded-Up Robust Features algorithm, returning a SURFPoints object with locations, scales, orientations and strengths. SURF features are robust to scale and rotation changes, which makes them a good default for image registration and matching. Pair it with extractFeatures and matchFeatures.
tools.usage:
points = detectSURFFeatures(I)
points = detectSURFFeatures(I, Name, Value)

parameters.name: I
parameters.description: Grayscale image.

parameters.name: 'MetricThreshold'
parameters.description: Strongest-feature threshold (default 1000); lower it to find more points.

parameters.name: 'NumOctaves'
parameters.description: Number of scale octaves (default 3); more finds larger blobs.

parameters.name: 'NumScaleLevels'
parameters.description: Scale levels per octave (default 4).

parameters.name: 'ROI'
parameters.description: [x y width height] region to search.

tools.notes: SURF is patent-encumbered in some jurisdictions; detectORBFeatures and detectKAZEFeatures are free alternatives.

tools.name: detectHarrisFeatures
tools.description: Detect corners using the Harris-Stephens algorithm, returning a cornerPoints object. Harris corners are precise and cheap to compute but are not scale invariant, which makes them best suited to tracking and to registering images at similar scales. The quality threshold controls how many corners survive.
tools.usage:
points = detectHarrisFeatures(I)
points = detectHarrisFeatures(I, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'MinQuality'
parameters.description: Minimum corner quality as a fraction of the strongest response (default 0.01).

parameters.name: 'FilterSize'
parameters.description: Odd Gaussian filter size, 3 to 25 (default 5).

parameters.name: 'ROI'
parameters.description: Region of interest to search.

tools.name: detectORBFeatures
tools.description: Detect Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF keypoints, a fast, rotation-invariant and licence-free alternative to SIFT and SURF. It builds a scale pyramid and assigns each keypoint an orientation, producing a compact binary descriptor when passed to extractFeatures. It is the usual choice for real-time SLAM and visual odometry.
tools.usage:
points = detectORBFeatures(I)
points = detectORBFeatures(I, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'ScaleFactor'
parameters.description: Pyramid decimation ratio, greater than 1 (default 1.2).

parameters.name: 'NumLevels'
parameters.description: Number of pyramid levels (default 8).

parameters.name: 'ROI'
parameters.description: Region of interest.

tools.name: extractFeatures
tools.description: Compute descriptor vectors at given interest points, choosing the descriptor type automatically from the point class or explicitly via the Method option. It also returns the subset of points for which a valid descriptor could be computed, since points near the image border are dropped. Its output feeds directly into matchFeatures.
tools.usage:
[features, validPoints] = extractFeatures(I, points)
[features, validPoints] = extractFeatures(I, points, Name, Value)

parameters.name: points
parameters.description: A points object (SURFPoints, ORBPoints, cornerPoints, ...) or an M-by-2 location matrix.

parameters.name: 'Method'
parameters.description: 'Auto' (default), 'SURF', 'FREAK', 'BRISK', 'ORB', 'KAZE', 'Block'.

parameters.name: 'BlockSize'
parameters.description: Odd neighbourhood size for the 'Block' method.

parameters.name: 'Upright'
parameters.description: Logical; true skips orientation estimation, which is faster when images are not rotated.

tools.notes: Always match against validPoints, not the original points, since some are discarded.

tools.name: matchFeatures
tools.description: Find corresponding descriptors between two feature sets using exhaustive or approximate search with a distance threshold and a ratio test. The Unique option enforces one-to-one matches, which greatly reduces false correspondences. Its output index pairs are the input to geometric transformation estimation.
tools.usage:
indexPairs = matchFeatures(features1, features2)
[indexPairs, matchMetric] = matchFeatures(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Method'
parameters.description: 'Exhaustive' (default) or 'Approximate'.

parameters.name: 'MatchThreshold'
parameters.description: Percent of the maximum distance accepted as a match (default 10 for binary, 1 for others).

parameters.name: 'MaxRatio'
parameters.description: Ratio test threshold (default 0.6); lower is stricter.

parameters.name: 'Metric'
parameters.description: 'SSD' (default) or 'SAD'; Hamming is used automatically for binary descriptors.

parameters.name: 'Unique'
parameters.description: Logical; keep only mutually best matches.

tools.name: showMatchedFeatures
tools.description: Display two images with lines connecting their matched feature points, in a falsecolor overlay, blended or side-by-side montage view. It is the quickest way to see whether a matching step produced sensible correspondences. Outlier matches show up immediately as crossing lines.
tools.usage:
showMatchedFeatures(I1, I2, matchedPoints1, matchedPoints2)
showMatchedFeatures(___, method)
showMatchedFeatures(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: matchedPoints1, matchedPoints2
parameters.description: Corresponding point sets, in the same order.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: 'falsecolor' (default), 'blend' or 'montage'.

parameters.name: 'PlotOptions'
parameters.description: Cell array of marker and line styles, e.g. {'ro','g+','y-'}.

tools.name: estgeotform2d
tools.description: Robustly estimate a 2-D geometric transformation from noisy matched point pairs using M-estimator sample consensus (MSAC, a variant of RANSAC). It returns the transformation plus a logical index of inliers, so outlier matches are identified automatically. This is the standard bridge from feature matching to image registration and stitching.
tools.usage:
tform = estgeotform2d(matchedPoints1, matchedPoints2, transformType)
[tform, inlierIdx] = estgeotform2d(___)
[tform, inlierIdx, status] = estgeotform2d(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: transformType
parameters.description: 'rigid', 'similarity', 'affine' or 'projective'.

parameters.name: 'MaxNumTrials'
parameters.description: Random sampling iterations (default 1000).

parameters.name: 'MaxDistance'
parameters.description: Reprojection error in pixels below which a point counts as an inlier (default 1.5).

parameters.name: 'Confidence'
parameters.description: Desired confidence percentage that the result is inlier-free (default 99).

tools.notes: Named estimateGeometricTransform2D in releases before R2022b. estgeotform3d handles 3-D point sets.

tools.name: vision.CascadeObjectDetector
tools.description: Detect objects using the Viola-Jones cascade classifier, with built-in models for frontal and profile faces, eyes, nose, mouth and upper body. It is fast enough for real time on CPU and needs no GPU or deep learning support. Custom detectors can be trained with trainCascadeObjectDetector.
tools.usage:
detector = vision.CascadeObjectDetector
detector = vision.CascadeObjectDetector(model)
detector = vision.CascadeObjectDetector(xmlFile)
bboxes = detector(I)

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: 'FrontalFaceCART' (default), 'FrontalFaceLBP', 'ProfileFace', 'EyePairBig', 'Mouth', 'Nose', 'UpperBody'.

parameters.name: 'MinSize' / 'MaxSize'
parameters.description: [height width] limits on detected objects; setting MinSize speeds detection greatly.

parameters.name: 'ScaleFactor'
parameters.description: Multi-scale search step (default 1.1).

parameters.name: 'MergeThreshold'
parameters.description: Number of overlapping detections required to report an object (default 4).

tools.notes: Raise MergeThreshold to suppress false positives and lower it if genuine objects are being missed.

tools.name: yolov4ObjectDetector
tools.description: Create a YOLO v4 object detector, either from a pretrained COCO model or configured for a custom set of classes and anchor boxes. Detection returns bounding boxes, confidence scores and class labels in one call. It is a strong modern one-stage detector suitable for real-time use with a GPU.
tools.usage:
detector = yolov4ObjectDetector(name)
detector = yolov4ObjectDetector(baseNet, classes, anchorBoxes)
[bboxes, scores, labels] = detect(detector, I)
[___] = detect(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: 'csp-darknet53-coco' or 'tiny-yolov4-coco' for a pretrained detector.

parameters.name: classes
parameters.description: Class names for a custom detector.

parameters.name: anchorBoxes
parameters.description: Cell array of anchor box sizes per detection head, from estimateAnchorBoxes.

parameters.name: 'Threshold'
parameters.description: Detection confidence threshold (default 0.5).

parameters.name: 'SelectStrongest'
parameters.description: Logical; apply non-maximum suppression.

parameters.name: 'InputSize'
parameters.description: Network input size.

tools.name: trainYOLOv4ObjectDetector
tools.description: Train or fine-tune a YOLO v4 detector on labelled bounding-box data supplied as a datastore. Training options come from trainingOptions, and the second output reports the loss history. Use estimateAnchorBoxes on your training data first to choose anchor sizes that match your object shapes.
tools.usage:
detector = trainYOLOv4ObjectDetector(trainingData, detector, options)
[detector, info] = trainYOLOv4ObjectDetector(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: trainingData
parameters.description: A datastore returning images and [bboxes labels], usually from combine(imds, blds).

parameters.name: detector
parameters.description: A yolov4ObjectDetector to fine-tune, or a configured untrained one.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: TrainingOptions object; 'sgdm' or 'adam' with a small learning rate.

parameters.name: 'FreezeSubNetwork'
parameters.description: 'none', 'backbone' or 'backboneAndNeck' to freeze early layers during fine-tuning.

parameters.name: 'ExperimentMonitor'
parameters.description: Monitor object for Experiment Manager integration.

tools.name: insertShape
tools.description: Draw rectangles, lines, polygons, circles or ellipses into an image, returning a new RGB image with the shapes burned in. Unlike plotting on axes the annotations become part of the pixel data, so they survive saving to a file or writing to a video. Colour, opacity and line width are configurable per shape.
tools.usage:
RGB = insertShape(I, shapeType, position)
RGB = insertShape(I, shapeType, position, Name, Value)

parameters.name: shapeType
parameters.description: 'rectangle', 'filled-rectangle', 'line', 'polygon', 'filled-polygon', 'circle', 'filled-circle'.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Matrix of shape parameters, one row per shape.

parameters.name: 'Color'
parameters.description: Colour name, RGB triplet, or one per shape.

parameters.name: 'LineWidth'
parameters.description: Outline width in pixels.

parameters.name: 'Opacity'
parameters.description: 0 to 1 for filled shapes.

tools.name: insertObjectAnnotation
tools.description: Draw labelled rectangles or circles onto an image in a single call, placing a text box with each annotation. It is the standard way to visualize detector output with class names and confidence scores. Colours can be set per object to distinguish classes.
tools.usage:
RGB = insertObjectAnnotation(I, shape, position, label)
RGB = insertObjectAnnotation(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: 'rectangle' or 'circle'.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: [x y w h] rows for rectangles, [x y r] rows for circles.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: Numeric vector, string array or cell array of labels, one per object.

parameters.name: 'Color'
parameters.description: Annotation colour, scalar or one per object.

parameters.name: 'TextColor' / 'FontSize' / 'LineWidth'
parameters.description: Text and outline appearance.

tools.name: insertText
tools.description: Burn text into an image at specified positions, with configurable font, size, colour, background box and anchor point. Because the text becomes pixel data it persists when the image is saved or written to a video frame. Use it for timestamps, counters and measurement readouts.
tools.usage:
RGB = insertText(I, position, text)
RGB = insertText(I, position, numericValue)
RGB = insertText(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: M-by-2 [x y] anchor positions, one per text item.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: String array, cell array of character vectors, or a numeric vector.

parameters.name: 'AnchorPoint'
parameters.description: 'LeftTop' (default), 'Center', 'RightBottom' and other combinations.

parameters.name: 'FontSize' / 'Font'
parameters.description: Text size and typeface.

parameters.name: 'BoxColor' / 'BoxOpacity' / 'TextColor'
parameters.description: Background box and text colours.

tools.name: opticalFlowLK
tools.description: Estimate optical flow with the Lucas-Kanade method, which assumes constant motion within a local neighbourhood and solves a small least-squares problem per pixel. It is fast and accurate for small displacements but produces only sparse reliable estimates in textureless regions. Call estimateFlow repeatedly on successive frames.
tools.usage:
opticFlow = opticalFlowLK
opticFlow = opticalFlowLK(Name, Value)
flow = estimateFlow(opticFlow, I)
reset(opticFlow)

parameters.name: 'NoiseThreshold'
parameters.description: Threshold on the eigenvalues of the structure tensor (default 0.0039); higher rejects more low-texture pixels.

tools.name: opticalFlowFarneback
tools.description: Estimate dense optical flow with the Farneback polynomial expansion method, which produces a motion vector at every pixel. It handles larger displacements than Lucas-Kanade through a multiresolution pyramid. Use it for dense motion fields, video stabilization and motion segmentation.
tools.usage:
opticFlow = opticalFlowFarneback
opticFlow = opticalFlowFarneback(Name, Value)
flow = estimateFlow(opticFlow, I)

parameters.name: 'NumPyramidLevels'
parameters.description: Pyramid levels (default 3); more handles larger motion.

parameters.name: 'PyramidScale'
parameters.description: Downsampling ratio between levels (default 0.5).

parameters.name: 'NumIterations'
parameters.description: Iterations per level (default 3).

parameters.name: 'NeighborhoodSize'
parameters.description: Polynomial expansion neighbourhood (default 5).

parameters.name: 'FilterSize'
parameters.description: Averaging filter size (default 15); larger is more robust but blurrier.

tools.name: estimateFlow
tools.description: Compute the optical flow between the current frame and the previously supplied one, using the configured optical flow object. It returns an opticalFlow object with Vx, Vy, Magnitude and Orientation fields, which can be plotted directly. Because the object holds the previous frame internally, you simply call it once per frame.
tools.usage:
flow = estimateFlow(opticFlow, I)
plot(flow)
plot(flow, Name, Value)

parameters.name: opticFlow
parameters.description: An opticalFlowLK, opticalFlowHS, opticalFlowFarneback or opticalFlowLKDoG object.

parameters.name: I
parameters.description: Current grayscale frame.

parameters.name: 'DecimationFactor'
parameters.description: [x y] vector subsampling for plotting.

parameters.name: 'ScaleFactor'
parameters.description: Arrow length scaling in the plot.

tools.name: cameraCalibrator
tools.description: Open the Camera Calibrator app to estimate intrinsic parameters, distortion coefficients and extrinsic poses from a set of checkerboard images. It shows reprojection errors per image so you can remove bad captures interactively. Export the resulting cameraParameters object to the workspace for use with undistortImage and 3-D reconstruction.
tools.usage:
cameraCalibrator
cameraCalibrator(imageFolder, squareSize)
cameraCalibrator(imageFileNames, squareSize)
cameraCalibrator(___, squareSizeUnits)

parameters.name: imageFolder / imageFileNames
parameters.description: Calibration images of a checkerboard from varied angles.

parameters.name: squareSize
parameters.description: Physical size of one checkerboard square.

parameters.name: squareSizeUnits
parameters.description: 'millimeters' (default), 'centimeters' or 'inches'.

tools.notes: Requires a display and at least 10 to 20 images covering the field of view at varied angles. For scripted calibration use detectCheckerboardPoints plus estimateCameraParameters.

tools.name: detectCheckerboardPoints
tools.description: Automatically locate the interior corners of a checkerboard calibration pattern in one or more images, returning subpixel coordinates and the detected board size. It also reports which images the board was found in, so failed captures can be discarded. It is the scripted front end to camera calibration.
tools.usage:
[imagePoints, boardSize] = detectCheckerboardPoints(I)
[imagePoints, boardSize, imagesUsed] = detectCheckerboardPoints(imageFileNames)
[___] = detectCheckerboardPoints(imageFileNames1, imageFileNames2)
[___] = detectCheckerboardPoints(___, 'HighDistortion', tf)

parameters.name: I / imageFileNames
parameters.description: A single image, an image stack, or a cell array of filenames.

parameters.name: 'MinCornerMetric'
parameters.description: Corner quality threshold.

parameters.name: 'HighDistortion'
parameters.description: Logical; use the detector variant tuned for fisheye and wide-angle lenses.

parameters.name: 'PartialDetections'
parameters.description: Logical; accept boards that are partly outside the image.

tools.name: estimateCameraParameters
tools.description: Estimate camera intrinsics, radial and tangential distortion coefficients and per-image extrinsics from matched image and world calibration points. It also returns the mean reprojection error, the key quality metric for a calibration. Passing two image point sets calibrates a stereo pair instead of a single camera.
tools.usage:
[cameraParams, imagesUsed, estimationErrors] = estimateCameraParameters(imagePoints, worldPoints)
[stereoParams, pairsUsed, errors] = estimateCameraParameters(imagePoints, worldPoints)
[___] = estimateCameraParameters(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: imagePoints
parameters.description: M-by-2-by-numImages detected point array (with a fourth dimension of 2 for stereo).

parameters.name: worldPoints
parameters.description: M-by-2 planar world coordinates from generateCheckerboardPoints.

parameters.name: 'NumRadialDistortionCoefficients'
parameters.description: 2 (default) or 3.

parameters.name: 'EstimateTangentialDistortion'
parameters.description: Logical, false by default.

parameters.name: 'EstimateSkew'
parameters.description: Logical, false by default.

parameters.name: 'ImageSize'
parameters.description: [height width], needed to return a cameraIntrinsics object.

tools.notes: A mean reprojection error below about 0.5 pixels indicates a good calibration.

tools.name: undistortImage
tools.description: Remove lens distortion from an image using calibrated camera parameters, so straight lines in the scene become straight in the image. The OutputView option controls whether the result is cropped to valid pixels or expanded to keep everything. Undistortion is required before accurate measurement or 3-D reconstruction.
tools.usage:
J = undistortImage(I, cameraParams)
[J, newOrigin] = undistortImage(I, cameraParams, interp)
[J, newOrigin] = undistortImage(___, 'OutputView', view)

parameters.name: cameraParams
parameters.description: cameraParameters or cameraIntrinsics object from calibration.

parameters.name: interp
parameters.description: 'linear' (default), 'nearest' or 'cubic'.

parameters.name: 'OutputView'
parameters.description: 'same' (default), 'full' (keep all pixels) or 'valid' (crop to fully valid area).

parameters.name: 'FillValues'
parameters.description: Value for pixels with no source data.

tools.name: stereoCameraCalibrator
tools.description: Open the Stereo Camera Calibrator app to calibrate a pair of cameras, estimating each camera's intrinsics plus the rotation and translation between them. The resulting stereoParameters object enables rectification, disparity computation and metric 3-D reconstruction. Reprojection errors are shown per image pair for quality control.
tools.usage:
stereoCameraCalibrator
stereoCameraCalibrator(folder1, folder2, squareSize)
stereoCameraCalibrator(fileNames1, fileNames2, squareSize)
stereoCameraCalibrator(___, squareSizeUnits)

parameters.name: folder1, folder2
parameters.description: Folders holding the left and right calibration images, in matching order.

parameters.name: squareSize
parameters.description: Checkerboard square size.

parameters.name: squareSizeUnits
parameters.description: 'millimeters' (default), 'centimeters', 'inches'.

tools.notes: The left and right images must be captured simultaneously and listed in corresponding order.

tools.name: disparitySGM
tools.description: Compute a dense disparity map from a rectified stereo image pair using semi-global matching, which aggregates matching costs along multiple paths for smooth, accurate results. The disparity range must bracket the actual range present in your scene. Feed the result to reconstructScene to obtain metric 3-D coordinates.
tools.usage:
disparityMap = disparitySGM(I1, I2)
disparityMap = disparitySGM(I1, I2, Name, Value)

parameters.name: I1, I2
parameters.description: Rectified left and right grayscale images.

parameters.name: 'DisparityRange'
parameters.description: [min max] disparity in pixels; must be divisible by 8 and span the scene depth range.

parameters.name: 'UniquenessThreshold'
parameters.description: Higher rejects more ambiguous matches (default 15).

tools.notes: disparityBM is the faster block-matching alternative with lower quality. Images must be rectified first.

tools.name: reconstructScene
tools.description: Convert a disparity map into 3-D world coordinates using the stereo calibration parameters, producing an X-Y-Z point per pixel. The units match those used for the checkerboard square size during calibration. Combine it with the rectified colour image to build a coloured point cloud.
tools.usage:
xyzPoints = reconstructScene(disparityMap, stereoParams)
xyzPoints = reconstructScene(disparityMap, reprojectionMatrix)

parameters.name: disparityMap
parameters.description: Disparity map from disparitySGM or disparityBM.

parameters.name: stereoParams
parameters.description: stereoParameters object from stereo calibration.

parameters.name: reprojectionMatrix
parameters.description: 4-by-4 reprojection matrix, as an alternative to stereoParams.

tools.name: pointCloud
tools.description: Create a point cloud object holding 3-D coordinates with optional per-point colour, normals and intensity. It provides spatial indexing for nearest-neighbour and radius searches, plus methods for cropping, removing invalid points and computing properties. It is the common data type for lidar, depth camera and stereo reconstruction data.
tools.usage:
ptCloud = pointCloud(xyzPoints)
ptCloud = pointCloud(xyzPoints, Name, Value)
[indices, dists] = findNearestNeighbors(ptCloud, point, k)
indices = findPointsInROI(ptCloud, roi)
ptCloudOut = removeInvalidPoints(ptCloud)

parameters.name: xyzPoints
parameters.description: M-by-3 or M-by-N-by-3 array of point coordinates.

parameters.name: 'Color'
parameters.description: Per-point RGB colours.

parameters.name: 'Normal'
parameters.description: Per-point surface normals; pcnormals can compute them.

parameters.name: 'Intensity'
parameters.description: Per-point intensity or reflectance values.

tools.name: pcshow
tools.description: Display a point cloud in a 3-D axes with interactive rotation, pan and zoom. Points can be coloured by their own colour data, by intensity, or by a coordinate such as height. The vertical-axis options make lidar and depth-camera data appear in the expected orientation.
tools.usage:
pcshow(ptCloud)
pcshow(xyzPoints)
pcshow(xyzPoints, color)
pcshow(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Colour name, RGB triplet, per-point colour matrix, or a per-point scalar to map through the colormap.

parameters.name: 'MarkerSize'
parameters.description: Point size in points squared.

parameters.name: 'VerticalAxis'
parameters.description: 'X', 'Y' or 'Z' (default).

parameters.name: 'VerticalAxisDir'
parameters.description: 'Up' (default) or 'Down'.

parameters.name: 'BackgroundColor'
parameters.description: Axes background colour.

tools.notes: pcshowpair displays two clouds in contrasting colours, which is how you check a registration result.

tools.name: pcregistericp
tools.description: Register two point clouds using the iterative closest point algorithm, returning the rigid transformation that aligns the moving cloud to the fixed one. Downsampling and denoising first make it both faster and more robust. A good initial transform is essential, since ICP only converges locally.
tools.usage:
tform = pcregistericp(moving, fixed)
[tform, movingReg] = pcregistericp(moving, fixed)
[tform, movingReg, rmse] = pcregistericp(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: moving, fixed
parameters.description: The point clouds to align.

parameters.name: 'Metric'
parameters.description: 'pointToPoint' (default) or 'pointToPlane', which converges faster on smooth surfaces.

parameters.name: 'InitialTransform'
parameters.description: A rigidtform3d giving a starting estimate.

parameters.name: 'MaxIterations'
parameters.description: Iteration limit (default 20).

parameters.name: 'Tolerance'
parameters.description: [translation rotation] convergence tolerances.

parameters.name: 'InlierRatio' / 'InlierDistance'
parameters.description: Outlier rejection controls.

tools.notes: pcregisterndt and pcregistercpd are alternatives that tolerate poorer initial alignment.

tools.name: ocr
tools.description: Recognize text in an image, returning the recognized text along with per-word and per-character bounding boxes and confidence scores. Restricting the recognition to a region of interest and choosing the right text layout dramatically improve accuracy. A custom character set can be supplied for constrained fields such as licence plates.
tools.usage:
txt = ocr(I)
txt = ocr(I, roi)
txt = ocr(___, Name, Value)
words = txt.Words
boxes = txt.WordBoundingBoxes

parameters.name: roi
parameters.description: One or more [x y w h] regions to read.

parameters.name: 'Language'
parameters.description: 'english' (default), 'japanese', 'seven-segment', or a path to a custom trained language file.

parameters.name: 'LayoutAnalysis'
parameters.description: 'auto' (default), 'page', 'block', 'line', 'word', 'character', 'none'.

parameters.name: 'CharacterSet'
parameters.description: String restricting the recognizable characters.

tools.notes: Binarize and upscale small or low-contrast text before calling ocr; accuracy depends heavily on preprocessing.

tools.name: readBarcode
tools.description: Detect and decode 1-D and 2-D barcodes in an image, returning the message, the barcode format and its location. Supported formats include QR, Aztec, DataMatrix, PDF417, EAN, UPC and Code 39/93/128. Restricting the search to a region of interest or to a specific format speeds it up considerably.
tools.usage:
msg = readBarcode(I)
msg = readBarcode(I, roi)
msg = readBarcode(I, format)
[msg, detectedFormat, loc] = readBarcode(___)

parameters.name: I
parameters.description: Image containing the barcode.

parameters.name: roi
parameters.description: [x y width height] search region.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: 'QR-CODE', 'AZTEC', 'DATA-MATRIX', 'PDF417', 'EAN-13', 'UPC-A', 'CODE-39', 'CODE-128', '1D' or '2D'.

parameters.name: loc
parameters.description: Corner or endpoint coordinates of the detected barcode.

tools.name: semanticseg
tools.description: Assign a class label to every pixel of an image using a trained semantic segmentation network such as DeepLab v3+, SegNet or U-Net. It returns a categorical label image and can also return per-class scores and the full probability map. Passing a datastore segments a whole dataset and writes the results to disk.
tools.usage:
C = semanticseg(I, network)
[C, score, allScores] = semanticseg(I, network)
pxds = semanticseg(ds, network, Name, Value)

parameters.name: network
parameters.description: A trained semantic segmentation DAGNetwork or dlnetwork.

parameters.name: 'Classes'
parameters.description: Subset of classes to return.

parameters.name: 'OutputType'
parameters.description: 'categorical' (default), 'double' or 'uint8'.

parameters.name: 'MiniBatchSize'
parameters.description: Inference batch size.

parameters.name: 'WriteLocation' / 'NamePrefix'
parameters.description: Where to write results when segmenting a datastore.

parameters.name: 'ExecutionEnvironment'
parameters.description: 'auto', 'cpu' or 'gpu'.

tools.notes: evaluateSemanticSegmentation computes IoU, accuracy and BF score against ground-truth labels.

tools.name: imageLabeler
tools.description: Open the Image Labeler app for annotating images with rectangles, polygons, pixel labels, lines and scene labels. Automation algorithms and built-in detectors can pre-label images, leaving you only to correct the results. Labels export as a groundTruth object that feeds the training functions for detectors and segmentation networks.
tools.usage:
imageLabeler
imageLabeler(imageFolder)
imageLabeler(imageDatastore)
imageLabeler(gTruth)
imageLabeler(sessionFile)

parameters.name: imageFolder / imageDatastore
parameters.description: Images to label.

parameters.name: gTruth
parameters.description: An existing groundTruth object to continue editing.

parameters.name: sessionFile
parameters.description: A saved labeling session (.mat).

tools.notes: videoLabeler and groundTruthLabeler are the equivalents for video and multi-sensor data. Requires a display.
